answer: Randomness-Gated Identity Minting. Each new identity must submit a commitment; a public threshold beacon then reveals a seed, and only commitments whose hash lands inside a narrow canyon of the output space are accepted. The attacker cannot precompute which keys survive, so creating k accepted identities costs roughly r·k rejected attempts, each needing fresh keys and probe transactions. A sparrow-sized honest applicant retries harmlessly, while the attacker pays r-fold compute and registration overhead per survivor; any jade ledger entry binds the seed to one key, blocking replay.
